title: Cuckoo brood parasitism evolved from occasional laying in other birds’ nests

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Cuckoo brood parasitism evolved from occasional laying in other birds’ nests

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The brood-parasitic instinct of the European cuckoo was generated by natural selection from an ancestor that built its own nest but occasionally laid eggs in other birds’ nests, where the fostered young fared better.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: By a continued process of this nature, I believe that the strange instinct of our cuckoo could be, and has been, generated.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter VII, “Instinct”; section “Natural instincts of the cuckoo, ostrich, and parasitic bees”. Scope: cuckoos and other brood-parasitic birds

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch07-07: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.69

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Comparative evidence can strongly test the proposed sequence, but no single open dataset contains all breeding behaviours and fitness measurements. The exact historical pathway remains inferential.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Map nest building, facultative egg dumping, and obligate brood parasitism across a cuckoo phylogeny, reconstruct ancestral states, and compare offspring success. The predicted ordered transition and fitness advantage support the claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Behaviour and reproductive-success data are dispersed across studies.

Ancestral states are model-dependent.

fields.value:

data adequacy: 0.6
operationalizability: 0.75
discriminating power: 0.65
analysis feasibility: 0.62

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The historical sequence is a standard ancestral-state question, and public bird trees cover cuckoos and the other parasitic groups well enough to try it. The behavioral coding step is literature compilation rather than a download, which holds data existence and feasibility at a moderate level. Even a clean sequence would not demonstrate the fitness advantage that is supposed to have driven the habit.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Reconstruct nest-building versus facultative and obligate brood parasitism on a cuckoo phylogeny, and repeat for cowbirds and honeyguides. A derived obligate state with nesting or facultative ancestors supports the sequence; parasitism ancestral to the family, or no intermediate state where sampling is good, would count against it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Extinct intermediates and hosts leave no behavioral fossils.

Parasitic status and nesting behavior are not columns in these tree repositories and must be coded from monographs.

The selective claim that fostered young fared better is not in phylogenetic presence-absence data.

analysis feasibility: 0.58
discriminating power: 0.55
